skill.name: nano-banana
skill.description: Generate and edit images with Google Gemini native image models through the inference.sh CLI.
skill.summary: Use inference.sh CLI commands to generate, edit, and configure Gemini image outputs.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation for using the inference.sh CLI with Gemini image models. Most static backtick findings are Markdown false positives, but several examples intentionally run infsh or npx commands and send prompt or image data to external services. No prompt injection or hidden exfiltration instructions were found.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed-tools to the specific infsh subcommands needed for image generation, if the platform supports narrower patterns.
Tell users that prompts, input images, image URLs, and search-grounded requests may be sent to inference.sh and Google services.
Use a bundled marketplace asset or trusted local image to avoid passive third-party image loads during rendering.

content.value_statement: Creating consistent Gemini image requests can be slow and error-prone. This skill provides ready CLI patterns for generation, editing, resolution, and grounding.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to run Gemini 3 Pro Image through the inference.sh CLI.
Shows how to run Gemini 2.5 Flash Image for faster generation.
Documents text-to-image prompts, image editing inputs, and multiple image outputs.
Lists supported options for aspect ratio, resolution, output format, and search grounding.
Provides sample workflows for generating input files and running edited requests.
limitations: Requires a working inference.sh CLI installation and account login.
Depends on remote inference.sh and Google model availability.
May send prompts, image URLs, and input images to external services.
Does not validate content policy, cost, quota, or license rights for generated images.

use_cases.title: Create campaign visuals
use_cases.description: Generate multiple image concepts with controlled aspect ratios and clear prompt structure.

use_cases.title: Edit source images
use_cases.description: Send an existing image reference with a natural language edit request through the CLI.

use_cases.title: Prototype visual workflows
use_cases.description: Compare Gemini image model options and build repeatable command-line image generation flows.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a simple image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana to create a square product concept image of a modern desk lamp on a clean studio background.

prompt_templates.title: Create multiple variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana to generate four logo concepts for a neighborhood bakery with warm colors and simple shapes.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an existing image
prompt_templates.scenario: Image editing with a source URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana to edit this image URL by replacing the cloudy sky with a bright sunset and keeping the foreground unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Build a grounded visual scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana with Google Search grounding to create a 16:9 editorial image based on current Tokyo weather conditions.

output_examples.input: A request for a photorealistic banana floating in space.
output_examples.output: A Gemini image generation run using the high quality model, with a concise prompt and standard output settings.

output_examples.input: A request to create four coffee shop logo options.
output_examples.output: A fast Gemini image run configured for multiple outputs, suitable for comparing visual directions.

output_examples.input: A request to add a rainbow to a landscape image.
output_examples.output: An image editing run that references the source image and applies the requested scene change.

best_practices: Confirm account login, expected cost, and model availability before running image jobs.
Use specific prompts with style, composition, lighting, and output requirements.
Avoid private, regulated, or licensed source images unless you have approval to process them externally.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad CLI commands without reviewing the exact model, input, and output settings.
Do not paste secrets, private customer data, or unreleased assets into prompts or image URLs.
Do not assume generated images are licensed for commercial use without separate review.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It provides inference.sh CLI examples for generating and editing images with Google Gemini image models.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require an external account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the inference.sh CLI and login before running model commands.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents an image editing workflow that passes input image references with an edit prompt.

faq.question: Can it use current information?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows a Google Search grounding option for prompts that need real-time context.

faq.question: What should users avoid?
faq.answer: Users should avoid sending sensitive prompts, private images, or unapproved licensed assets to external services.
